tools.name: web_scrape
tools.description: Processes a page and returns every output you ask for at once: markdown, html, links, screenshot, PDF, accessibility tree, elements by selector, AI-structured data, and `controls` (what can be clicked). One call, and a partial failure does not void the rest. From 1 credit ($0.002) per output. A url

tools.name: web_session_open
tools.description: Opens a browser session and returns the map of controls. Opening costs 2.5 credits plus the requested outputs; the first minute is included. Further started minutes cost 2 credits with an account key. Use web_act to interact and web_session_close when done. API key and credits required. Reference: h

tools.name: web_act
tools.description: Runs actions against an open session and returns the resulting state. Actions: {navigate}, {click:{ref}}, {type:{ref,text,clear}}, {select:{ref,value}}, {press}, {scroll}, {wait}, {back}. The `ref` is the one `controls` gave you. It stops at the first failure and tells you where. $0.0005 (0.25 credi

tools.name: web_scrape_batch
tools.description: A batch OF SCRAPES: reads a list of urls YOU give it (2 to 50, from any sites) and returns a jobId. It discovers nothing on its own — for that use web_crawl. API key and credits required. Poll it with web_batch_status.

tools.name: web_batch_status
tools.description: Checks a batch of scrapes: status, how many are done, and the results. Free for the owning account. Pass `cancel: true` to stop it.

tools.name: web_map
tools.description: Every url of a site, fast and cheap: its sitemap plus, optionally, the links on the page. Use it BEFORE crawling, to see what is there and decide what is worth reading. 1 credit ($0.002) with `includePage: false` (no browser at all), 1.5 credits ($0.003) with the page. Reference for the oassis API:

tools.name: web_crawl
tools.description: Follows a site's links and reads every page. Returns a jobId; poll it with web_crawl_status. API key and credits required; `limit` controls the maximum pages charged. Use web_map first if you only need the urls. Reference for the oassis API: https://oassis.dev/openapi.json

tools.name: web_crawl_status
tools.description: Checks a crawl: status, pages read, discovered and still queued, and the pages themselves. Free for the owning account. Pass `cancel: true` to stop it.

tools.name: web_search_exa
tools.description: Search the web with Exa's index: a query instead of a url, for when you do not know where to look. Returns title, url and a snippet per result. To read the pages, pass the urls to web_scrape_batch. The engine is named because the price is Exa's, passed through with no markup and read from its own pa

tools.name: web_feedback
tools.description: Tell us an answer was good or bad. FREE. Use it when a result is wrong — empty markdown, a control map missing a button, data that does not match the page — with the url or the jobId so it can be reproduced. It is the only way we learn that we read a page badly: our logs cannot tell that apart from

tools.name: web_task_start
tools.description: Starts a research task: a question answered by reading public pages, with sources, progress and cost. Requires an API key and credits. The maximum budget is reserved, actual execution cost is charged, and unused credits are released. Returns a task id: check it with web_task_status.

tools.name: web_task_status
tools.description: Returns a task's status, progress, sources, limitations, result and billing. Only your own tasks.

tools.name: web_task_cancel
tools.description: Stops a task using its owning API key, or its legacy access_token. No new operations start. Cancellation is free; unused account credit reservations are released. Cancelling a finished task changes nothing.

tools.name: web_session_close
tools.description: Closes the browser session and stops its time. HTTP equivalent: POST /web/v1/session/{id}/close. No additional close fee; outstanding browser time is settled when applicable. If you do not close it, it closes itself after a minute without use.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "web_task_cancel" references sensitive artifacts (access_token). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Stops a task using its owning API key, or its legacy access_token. No new operations start. Cancellation is free; unused account credit reservations are release…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: web_scrape, web_scrape_batch, web_crawl, web_search_exa, web_feedback · Private data: web_scrape, web_session_open, web_act, web_scrape_batch, web_crawl, web_search_exa, web_task_start, web_task_cancel · Public sink: web_session_close.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: web_scrape, web_scrape_batch, web_crawl, web_search_exa, web_feedback · Private data: web_scrape, web_session_open, web_act, web_scrape_batch, web_crawl, web_search_exa, web_task_start, web_task_cancel · Public sink: web_session_close

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
